title: Functoriality of the maps on cohomology induced by f-maps
statement: Maps on cohomology induced by $h$-maps are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. (1) (Independence.) $\varphi^*$ does not depend on the choices of resolutions and of $\beta$. (2) (Composition.) Let $h:X\to Y$ and $k:Y\to Z$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal H$, $\mathcal G$, $\mathcal F$ modules on $Z$, $Y$, $X$, and $\psi:\mathcal H\to k_*\mathcal G$, $\varphi:\mathcal G\to h_*\mathcal F$ an $k$-map and an $h$-map. Then $k_*(\varphi)\circ\psi:\mathcal H\to k_*h_*\mathcal F=(k\circ h)_*\mathcal F$ is a $(k\circ h)$-map and $(k_*(\varphi)\circ\psi)^*=\varphi^*\circ\psi^*:H^p(Z,\mathcal H)\to H^p(X,\mathcal F)$ for all $p\ge0$. In particular ($h$ or $k$ the identity) $\varphi^*\circ H^p(u)=(\varphi\circ u)^*$ and $H^p(v)\circ\varphi^*=(h_*(v)\circ\varphi)^*$ for morphisms of modules $u$, $v$ on $Y$, $X$; and for the pullbacks of modules [def-pc-module-pullback] $(k\circ h)^*=H^p(c)\circ h^*\circ k^*$ with $c:h^*k^*\mathcal H\cong(k\circ h)^*\mathcal H$ the canonical isomorphism. (3) (Restriction.) In the situation of (2) with $h$ omitted, for an open $V\subseteq Z$ and $W=k^{-1}(V)$, restricting to $V$ and $W$ [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap] (b) commutes with $\psi^*$: $\mathrm{res}_W\circ\psi^*=(\psi|_V)^*\circ\mathrm{res}_V$, where $\psi|_V:\mathcal H|_V\to(k|_W)_*(\mathcal G|_W)$ is the restriction of $\psi$ (a special case of (2)).

source.place: Cohomology of Sheaves, Section 01F7 (section-functoriality): Lemma 01F8 ('this construction is functorial in the triple') and Remark 01FB (independence of the choices); the composition rule is used without statement in Stacks (statement assembled by the agent)
